wins: Seeded accurate network reconnaissance data (nmap -sC -sV) for the target subnet, confirming live host list and service versions.
Identified web server running outdated Apache 2.4.49 with directory listing enabled, enabling targeted src exposure.
fails: SSH pivot attempt failed due to enforced MFA, preventing credential harvesting toward lateral movement.
Exploit stage stalled because elevated shell was unavailable; privilege escalation via CVE-2021-41773 not achieved.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance and initial enumeration completed, but exploitation and lateral objectives remain unmet; need targeted exploitation path.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Failure to escalate privileges on the Apache web server despite known CVE, likely due to missing proof-of-concept adaptation.

skill_cards.if_condition: When web server enumerated with Apache 2.4.49 and directory listing enabled
skill_cards.then_action: Gather directory contents with curl/wget and search for sensitive configs before attempting exploits

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is open but requires MFA
skill_cards.then_action: Collect hostkeys and banners then pivot to web-based exploit vector instead of forcing brute-force
Execute tailored exploit with curl -k to trigger path traversal (CVE-2021-41773) and verify file retrieval

memory_ops.reason: Consistent success collecting directories that inform later exploit development.

next_experiments.title: CVE-2021-41773 Proof-of-Concept
next_experiments.description: Craft curl request with encoded path traversal payload to retrieve /etc/passwd, validate exploitability before shell attempts.

next_experiments.title: Credential harvesting from exposed configs
next_experiments.description: Use dirb/ffuf on webroot to find config files, then parse for plaintext creds to try SSH or local traversal.

next_experiments.title: Pivot strategy via web shell
next_experiments.description: If traversal succeeds, upload PHP web shell and enumerate local creds/environment before attempting privilege escalation.
